title: Missing Rate Limiting and Brute Force Protection on Login Endpoint
description: The login endpoint (/login) does not implement any rate limiting, account lockout, or brute force protection mechanisms. An attacker can submit unlimited login attempts without any throttling, delays, or account lockout after multiple failed attempts. This makes the endpoint vulnerable to credential stuffing and brute force attacks where attackers can test common passwords against known usernames or use compromised credential lists without detection or account lockout.
impact:
Attackers can perform brute force attacks to compromise user accounts by:
1. Testing common passwords against known usernames without rate limiting
2. Using credential stuffing attacks with large compromised credential lists
3. Testing weak passwords without detection, delays, or account lockout
4. Performing distributed attacks without per-IP or per-session rate limiting
5. Conducting automated password guessing against multiple accounts simultaneously

This could lead to unauthorized access to user accounts and potential compromise of the entire application, especially when combined with exposed credentials or default credentials found in the application.
evidence:
POC testing confirmed:
- Sent 12 consecutive failed login attempts with different passwords
- All 12 requests returned HTTP 200 with response times: Min=9ms, Max=77ms (68ms range)
- No X-RateLimit-*, Retry-After, or other rate limiting headers present in responses
- No progressive delays between requests - responses are fast and consistent
- No account lockout message detected after multiple failed attempts
- No per-IP rate limiting or request throttling observed
- Credential stuffing simulation with 5 common passwords (password123, admin123, 123456, qwerty, letmein) all rejected quickly (8-48ms) without throttling
- Request/Response pattern: Each request accepted within milliseconds, returns "Invalid username or password" consistently
- Endpoint continues accepting requests indefinitely without any protective mechanisms

POC Output Summary:
✗ No rate limiting headers detected
✗ No progressive delays - responses are fast and consistent (9-77ms across all attempts)
✗ No account lockout detected after multiple failures
✗ Endpoint accepts unlimited credential attempts without throttling
✗ Fast response times enable efficient brute forcing and credential stuffing
remediation:
1. Implement rate limiting at the application level using libraries like Flask-Limiter:
   - Limit login attempts to 5 attempts per minute per IP address
   - Implement progressive backoff - increase delays after each failed attempt

2. Implement account lockout mechanism:
   - Lock account after N failed attempts (recommend 5 failed attempts)
   - Implement time-based lockout (e.g., 15-minute lockout period)
   - Notify user of lockout via email with unlock instructions

3. Implement CAPTCHA challenge:
   - Present CAPTCHA after 3 failed attempts to prevent automated attacks
   - Use reCAPTCHA v3 for invisible verification

4. Implement per-IP rate limiting:
   - Track and limit requests from the same IP address
   - Block IPs after excessive failed attempts
   - Implement exponential backoff or sliding window rate limiting

5. Implement security monitoring and logging:
   - Log all failed authentication attempts with timestamp, IP, username
   - Alert on multiple failed attempts from same IP
   - Alert on attempts using common passwords

6. Additional security measures:
   - Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) to reduce password compromise impact
   - Monitor for distributed brute force attacks (same password across multiple accounts)
   - Use HTTPS only (already recommended in other findings)
   - Implement secure session management (already recommended in other findings)
references: OWASP A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures, CWE-307 (Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames), CWE-521 (Weak Password Requirements), CWE-613 (Insufficient Session Expiration), OWASP Testing Guide - Testing for Weak or Unenforced Username Policy, OWASP Cheat Sheet - Authentication Cheat Sheet
toolCallDescription: Documenting finding: Missing Rate Limiting and Brute Force Protection - HIGH severity issue with working POC demonstrating unlimited login attempts, no delays, no account lockout
